title: A failure to explain
goal: A task row's findings badge names the mildest finding instead of the worst: a task whose handoff holds a major and an info finding shows 'info'. The core test 'labels a severity, and names the worst one a row can show' in packages/core/src/models/__tests__/Handoff.test.ts fails, and so does 'carries the summary, the whole finding count and the worst severity the digest keeps' in packages/core/src/taskRow/__tests__/taskRow.test.ts. Find the cause and fix it so that both tests pass without changing what they expect.

patches.find: if (worst === null || SEVERITY_RANK[severity] < SEVERITY_RANK[worst]) worst = severity;
patches.replace: if (worst === null || SEVERITY_RANK[severity] > SEVERITY_RANK[worst]) worst = severity;

failingTest.name: labels a severity, and names the worst one a row can show

integrationRisks: A fix guessed without reproducing, which may 'fix' the test instead of the code.
Hypotheses investigated inside the fix task, or by the planner reading the whole of core itself.
A fix that names the cause but never runs the two failing tests, so nothing shows it held.
key.expectedStrategy: Reproduce first (the planner running the failing tests itself, a script or read-only task running them, or the fix task running them before it changes code). If the planner found the cause, one fix task that names it (Handoff.ts, worstSeverity and the rank comparison) and validates with the two named tests is enough; if it did not, research tasks each testing a hypothesis, then the fix depending on them, verified by the same tests.
